predecessors.name: Qing dynasty
predecessors.text: Jintian in Guiping county, Guangxi, where the Jintian Uprising began in January 1851 (approximate position of Guiping)

successors.name: Qing dynasty
successors.text: Nanjing (Tianjing) and the lower Yangtze land still held in 1864, retaken by Qing armies; Hong Tianguifu was captured on 25 October 1864 and the last Taiping army was wiped out in August 1871

ledger.x: 1851: Hong Xiuquan proclaims the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom at Jintian in Guangxi.
1852: the Taiping army marches north through Hunan and takes Wuchang on the Yangtze.
1853: Anqing falls to the Taiping in February.
1853: the Taiping take Nanjing and make it their capital, Tianjing.
1858: the rest of Jiangxi falls to the Xiang Army by September.
1860: the Taiping break the siege of Nanjing and take Hangzhou on 19 March, Changzhou on 26 May and Suzhou on 2 June.
1861: the Xiang Army captures Anqing with a Royal Navy blockade, around the death of the Xianfeng Emperor.
1861: the Eastern Expedition takes Ningbo on 9 December and Hangzhou on 31 December.
1862: the attack on Shanghai is beaten.
1862: Ningbo is retaken on 10 May with the help of the Ever Victorious Army.
1864: Qing armies reconquer the Taiping land in Jiangsu and Zhejiang outside Nanjing (Suzhou, Changzhou, Hangzhou).
1864: Nanjing falls on 19 July and the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom ends.

wars.name: Taiping Rebellion
wars.outcome: Qing victory: Nanjing fell on 19 July 1864 and the Heavenly Kingdom ended; remnants were hunted down until January 1866 and a last army was destroyed in August 1871.

wars.name: Taiping Northern Expedition
wars.outcome: Failure: 'The attempt to take Beijing failed'; 'The Northern expedition was a complete failure'.

wars.name: Taiping Western Expedition
wars.outcome: Limited success: 'the Western achieved limited success'; the Taiping held Wuchang until December 1856 and Jiangxi until 1858.

wars.name: Battle of Shanghai (1860-1862)
wars.outcome: Repulsed: Chinese and European forces defeated the Taiping attempts on Shanghai; the Ever Victorious Army, named by the Qing in March 1862, 'repulsed another attack on Shanghai in 1862'.

wars.name: Third Battle of Nanking
wars.outcome: Qing victory: investment completed 2 March 1864; the city fell on 19 July 1864 and burned until 26 July; Li Xiucheng was captured on 22 July; over 200,000 Taiping troops surrendered.

certainty.note: A rebel state with moving fronts: the Taiping held cities and the roads between them, and the pages give no boundary lines.
